context: Official SBI, SBI VC Trade, Ripple and Visa disclosures establish multiple direct XRP, XRPL, RLUSD, USDC, JPYSC and Circle Arc relationships. The same group participates across several payment and asset rails.
decision: Model SBI Group as a multi-rail financial group, not an exclusive Ripple or Circle proxy.
Separate SBI Remit's explicit XRP ODL bridge-asset remittance use from SBI Ripple Asia's XRPL tokenized-deposit concept proof, which does not establish native XRP use.
Separate SBI VC Trade's Ethereum-only RLUSD distribution from XRPL RLUSD availability; no SBI-mediated XRPL RLUSD flow is established at launch.
Treat SBI VC Trade's USDC and RLUSD as coexisting USD stablecoin distribution, not an exclusive issuer relationship.
Keep JPYSC distinct from JPYC. SBI Shinsei Trust Bank issues JPYSC; Circle StableFX lists JPYC but not JPYSC; no JPYSC StableFX route is established.

Treat Visa card rewards, SBI START bond XRP benefits and term-deposit coupons as acquisition incentives, not measured net new market purchases. Record amounts, dates, eligibility and expiry separately.
Treat the SBI VC Trade two-million account figure as registered distribution reach, not active users, XRP holders or XRP liquidity.
Treat the SBI Ripple Asia 60% figure as SBI Group voting rights in the joint venture, not ownership of Ripple Labs.
Preserve SBIC East Japan as distinct from SBI Group; no relationship is inferred.
Do not admit these announcements as price-predictive features without actual volume, synchronized timestamps, fixed-horizon outcomes and out-of-sample validation.
invariants: No market-flow claim without transaction, reserve or issuer data that establishes actual capital movement.
A chain integration is not proof of native XRP demand.
A stablecoin listing is not proof of collateral deployment or bridge-asset use.
A reward program is not proof of an open-market purchase.
Historical corridor launch evidence is not current corridor volume.
DESIGNED, EXECUTED and VERIFIED remain distinct.
No forecast without fixed target/horizon/cutoff, assumptions, probability, alternatives and later outcome.
